metadata.title: Conformally Sasakian manifolds and the $k$-nullity condition
metadata.abstract: We study almost contact metric manifolds that are locally conformal to Sasakian manifolds in the normalization of Olszak. We show that the local conformal factors are uniquely determined by the structure; consequently, every such manifold is globally conformal to a Sasakian manifold and its Lee form is exact. We then investigate the $k$-nullity condition $ R(X,Y)\xi=k\{\eta(Y)X-\eta(X)Y\}. $ We prove that a smooth nullity function is necessarily constant, including in dimension three. Moreover, the $k$-nullity condition is equivalent to the assertion that $f=\exp(\sigma)$ satisfies $ \mathrm{Hess}_g f=-(kf+C)g $ for a constant $C$, and hence to the fact that the conformal metrics $g$ and $g_0=\exp(-2\sigma)g$ have the same geodesic circles. We derive the range of the conformal factor, a local warped-product description, and a classification in the complete case: when the Lee form is nonzero, the complete metric is a simply connected space form of curvature $k$. Finally, we construct incomplete examples of nonconstant sectional curvature in every dimension $2n+1\geq 5$.

metadata.title: Geometric Hammocks: Surface Laminations and the Ziegler Spectrum of String Algebras
metadata.abstract: We give the first complete topological, geometric, and ergodic classification of the Ziegler spectrum $\Zg(\Lambda)$ of a non-domestic string algebra $\Lambda$ over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary cardinality, via a dictionary with Thurston's theory of geodesic laminations on a cusped hyperbolic surface. This is a model-theoretic counterpart of Haiden--Katzarkov--Kontsevich's realization (\emph{Publ.\ Math.\ IHES} 2017) of stability conditions on the bounded derived category of a gentle algebra via flat surfaces: pure-injective modules correspond to admissible geodesics, and the Ziegler topology to a corridor quotient of Chabauty space. Three consequences follow. The Krull--Gabriel dimension equals the surface's topological accumulation depth, and the string closure with all higher Cantor--Bendixson strata is globally homeomorphic to an explicit corridor space, with the pushout map to $\Zg(\Lambda)$ a homeomorphism if and only if $\Lambda$ is domestic. Prefix-free dyadic blocks in the geometric perfect core verify Puninski's cardinality-free two-chain criterion, resolving the open problem of superdecomposable pure-injectives over uncountable fields for all non-domestic string and special biserial algebras. Three purely algebraic invariants on the perfect core---localized pp-shape entropy, a $K_0$-weighted pressure function satisfying an algebraic Ruelle--Walters Variational Principle, and a pp-bifurcation index with a Gauss--Bonnet simplicity obstruction---strictly separate uncountable iso-entropic and iso-pressure families, and the inverse limit of the quotient pp-lattice recovers the transversal Cantor cross-section.

metadata.title: On the Concavity of Rényi Entropy and Rényi Entropy Power along Heat Flows on Manifolds
metadata.abstract: In this paper, we establish the concavity of Rényi entropy and Rényi entropy power along heat flow on Euclidean space of arbitrary dimension, for Rényi orders $\alpha\in[1,2]$. More generally, we prove the corresponding result along the heat flow generated by the Witten Laplacian on complete Riemannian manifolds under a suitable curvature-dimension condition. Our argument builds on novel functional inequalities that were recently developed for the study of Tsallis entropy concavity along the heat flow. We extend both these inequalities and the resulting concavity theorem from the Euclidean setting to the Riemannian manifold setting. In addition, we establish the complete monotonicity of Tsallis entropy of order $2$ along the heat flow and derive its spectral decomposition.

metadata.title: Vanishing Theorem of Pin(2)-equivariant Bauer-Furuta Invariants as Stable Sections
metadata.abstract: We develop a viewpoint of Pin(2)-equivariant Bauer-Furuta invariant: It can be converted to a section over a finite dimensional Pin(2)-orbit, and it takes values in ordinary stable homotopy class. This viewpoint reveals a topological limitation of the invariant: If the fiber's connectivity exceeds the dimension of the base space, then all sections are homotopic to the trivial section. We use it to recover Lin-Mukherjee vanishing theorem. Furthermore, the family Seiberg-Witten invariant can be obtained from the pullback of such sections to $S^1$-orbit. We use this fact to prove a vanishing theorem of the Pin(2)-equivariant family Bauer-Furuta invariant after two stabilizations.

metadata.title: Thompson indices of knots and the invertibility problem
metadata.abstract: Jones showed that Thompson's group $F$ produces all unoriented links, and introduced its oriented subgroup $\vec{F}$, which produces all oriented links; the same holds for the Brown-Thompson group $F_3$ and its oriented subgroup $\vec{F}_3$. The corresponding Thompson indices measure the complexity of a knot in these groups, much as the braid index does for braid groups. In this article we prove that the span of the Jones polynomial plus $1$ is a lower bound for the $F$- and $\vec{F}$-index, and we give lower bounds for the $\vec{F}$- and $\vec{F}_3$-index in terms of the degrees of the HOMFLY-PT polynomial. We then compute the four indices (the $F$-, $F_3$-, $\vec{F}$- and $\vec{F}_3$-index) for the prime knots with at most 13 crossings, by an exhaustive enumeration of tree diagrams (up to 13 leaves for $F$, 17 for $\vec{F}$, with the HOMFLY-PT polynomials of all the diagrams with 19 leaves, and 9 and 11 for $F_3$ and $\vec{F}_3$) completed by targeted searches; every value is rigorously certified, by exact computations and by verified computations of hyperbolic structures in interval arithmetic. The $F$-index is determined for all knots with at most 11 crossings, the $\vec{F}$-index for all knots with at most 8 crossings, and the $F_3$- and $\vec{F}_3$-index for all knots with at most 12 crossings. The main outcome of these computations is that the oriented indices are sensitive to the orientation: we find hundreds of non-invertible knots $K$ whose reverse $K^r$ has a different $\vec{F}$- or $\vec{F}_3$-index, the smallest being $8_{17}$ (with $\vec{F}_3$-index $7$ and $9$). The $\vec{F}$-index also distinguishes the Conway knot from its mutant, the Kinoshita-Terasaka knot.

metadata.title: Every hyperbolic knot has an arc-faithful closed braid diagram
metadata.abstract: Every hyperbolic knot admits an arc-faithful closed braid diagram, answering Conjecture 29 of McPhail-Snyder. More precisely, any braid representing the knot can be reworded in the same braid group so that the complete holonomy has distinct incoming parabolic fixed points at every crossing. The construction replaces a pinched crossing by five non-pinched crossings when a suitable third strand is adjacent. On $n$ strands it uses at most $2n-1$ letters per replaced crossing. The resulting diagram realizes the complete holonomy by nondegenerate shapes in its four-term octahedral decomposition.

metadata.title: VC-Dimension and Generalization in Geometric Machine Learning with Applications to Active Learning
metadata.abstract: We compute the VC-dimension of metric ball classifiers in the model spaces of Riemannian geometry (Euclidean, spherical, hyperbolic) and present upper and lower bounds on the VC-dimension of metric balls in several other situations, including general normed vector spaces (potentially infinite VC-dimension), vector spaces with $\ell^p$-norms (VC-dimension grows at least linearly in the dimension, faster than Euclidean for $p=1$), flat tori, and general Riemannian manifolds (arbitrarily large VC-dimension after a conformal change). In several situations where the VC-dimension is large or even infinite, we prove generalization bounds under additional assumptions on the data distribution using covering arguments. Both in the VC-dimension and covering setting, we consider data on low-dimensional subsets of high-dimensional Euclidean spaces. As an application, we consider coverage-based algorithms in active learning.

metadata.title: Branching Pattern Modeling: A Geometric Measure Theory Approach
metadata.abstract: This article is based on a lecture given at Westlake University. It aims to introduce students to an application of geometric measure theory in modeling branched patterns found in both living and nonliving systems. We begin with the Eulerian framework of ramified optimal transportation, including discrete transport paths, their basic properties, numerical approximation, and the passage to general transport paths represented by rectifiable currents. We then describe an application to the dynamic formation of a plant leaf, where branching venation patterns arise from a balance between metabolic benefit and transportation cost. Finally, we review landscape functions associated with transport paths and explain how two existing approaches can be unified within a broader family of rectifiable $1$-currents. We conclude by indicating several open directions related to Gilbert-type network problems, biological modeling, and numerical approximation.

metadata.title: A Topological Approach to the Discrete Dual Minkowski Problem
metadata.abstract: The discrete dual Minkowski problem asks for the necessary and sufficient conditions on a finite discrete measure $\mu$ on $S^{n-1}$ such that $\mu$ is given by the $q^{th}$ dual curvature measure of a convex polytope in $\mathbb{R}^n$. In this paper, using topological degree theory, a novel framework is developed to prove existence of solutions. This approach is applied to the case of polytopes in $\mathbb{R}^n$ for $q>0$ and $n\geq 2$ whose outer normals are in general position while also subject to a constraint on their distribution on $S^{n-1}$. Moreover, existence of solutions is also proved in the plane under a different constraint on the outer normals by proving that a family of non-linear second-order recurrence relations do not have non-constant $N$-periodic solutions.

metadata.title: Surface subgroups with prescribed finite quotients
metadata.abstract: We prove that every finite quotient of a finite covolume Kleinian group $G$ can be realized by a surface subgroup. More precisely, given an epimorphism from $G$ onto a finite group $F$, there exists a surface subgroup that maps surjectively onto $F$. As a consequence, the union of the surface subgroups is dense in $G$ with respect to the profinite topology. We also apply this result to obtain more examples of atoroidal surface bundles with signature zero in the construction of Kent--Leininger.

metadata.title: Covering the Triangular Lattice with Non-Overlapping Unit Disks
metadata.abstract: For $d>0$, let $\mathcal{T}_d$ be the triangular lattice with minimum distance $d$. We study for which $d$ the set $\mathcal{T}_d$ can be covered by closed unit disks with pairwise disjoint interiors, a question left open by Phetmak, Nuntasombat and Fakcharoenphol for $2-\sqrt3\le d<2/\sqrt{37}$ and on several gaps between their constructions. Writing $\mathcal{N}(d)$ for the largest number of points of $\mathcal{T}_d$ in a closed unit disk, we show that $\mathcal{T}_d$ cannot be covered whenever $\mathcal{N}(d)<4/d^2$, and we determine this set of spacings exactly as a union of fifteen intervals; combined with their constructions, this shows that coverability is not monotone in $d$. At the right endpoints $d=2/\sqrt k$ of these intervals the density bound is attained, and we show that such a spacing is coverable if and only if $k$ is the norm of an Eisenstein integer. We also give two new coverings, at $d=1/\sqrt{13}$ and $d=2/\sqrt{21}$, in which the disks form a hexagonal packing. Consequently, together with an earlier result of Okayama, Kiyomi and Uehara, the smallest coverable spacing $d_{\min}$ exists and satisfies $2/\sqrt{55}<d_{\min}\le1/\sqrt{13}$, which answers a question of Phetmak, Nuntasombat and Fakcharoenphol.

metadata.title: First-order asymptotic expansions for spectral convergence of normalized graph Laplacians constructed from samples on manifolds
metadata.abstract: Under i.i.d. uniform sampling from a closed Riemannian manifold embedded in Euclidean space, we derive first-order asymptotic expansions for the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of symmetrically normalized graph Laplacians constructed via Gaussian kernels and provide concentration inequalities for the remainder terms. As a direct consequence, we establish the corresponding weak convergence results. Unlike most related works, our analysis does not impose a multiplicity-one assumption on the eigenvalues, thereby extending the applicability of the framework to general manifolds with potentially nontrivial eigenvalue multiplicities.

metadata.title: Convex monohedral tilings: a sharp neighbor bound and rigidity in the equality case
metadata.abstract: We study both side-to-side and non-side-to-side convex monohedral tilings of the Euclidean plane in which every tile has the same number of neighbors. Reflections are allowed, point contacts count as neighbors, and no periodicity assumption is imposed. Combining boundary estimates for sums of face curvatures, angle-incidence counts and side-length matching, we prove that the common neighbor number satisfies $N\le21$ and classify all equality cases. Equality holds precisely when the prototile is a $30^\circ$-$30^\circ$-$120^\circ$ triangle and the entire tiling is similar to the central subdivision of the standard equilateral triangular tiling. This resolves the open problem on the maximum common number of neighbors recorded in Adams's The Tiling Book.

metadata.title: Combinatorial curvature flows for spherical vertex scalings on infinitely triangulated surfaces
metadata.abstract: We study the combinatorial Yamabe and Calabi flows for spherical vertex scalings on infinitely triangulated surfaces. Under the assumptions of uniformly bounded vertex degree and an $\epsilon$-uniformly nondegenerate initial metric, we establish the short-time existence of smooth solutions to both combinatorial curvature flows. We also establish short-time uniqueness for the combinatorial Yamabe flow. For the combinatorial Calabi flow, we establish short-time uniqueness among solutions that are continuous in time with respect to the $L^\infty(V)$ norm.

metadata.title: Morse index and bifurcation of Clifford hypersurfaces under Hopf squashing
metadata.abstract: Clifford hypersurfaces are products of two spheres embedded in a round sphere. We call them balanced when their radii are chosen so that the product is minimal in the round metric. We study how their Morse index and nullity change when the ambient metric is deformed along the fibers of a Hopf fibration. This deformation, called \emph{Hopf squashing}, rescales the fiber metric by a parameter $t>0$ while leaving the horizontal metric unchanged. For the complex, quaternionic, and octonionic Hopf fibrations, we determine the index and nullity of balanced Clifford hypersurfaces throughout the fiber-shortening range and show that their Jacobi potential is independent of $t$. In the octonionic case we also determine the first positive Jacobi eigenvalue and its multiplicity. In the octonionic case, at $t=27$, a branch of nonhomogeneous minimal hypersurfaces bifurcates from the balanced Clifford hypersurface; its members have Morse index $1432$ and nullity $15$.

metadata.title: Generalized Frobenius manifolds: symmetries and their classification in 2-dimensions
metadata.abstract: A theory of symmetries of generalized Frobenius manifolds is developed. This is used to study the solution space of all generalized Frobenius manifolds that are "above" a specific Frobenius manifold. Since all (semi-simple) Frobenius manifolds in 2-dimensions are known, by constructing all homogeneous Legendre fields associated to these manifolds we classify all 2-dimensional generalized Frobenius manifolds. With this description, the known examples of generalized Frobenius manifolds correspond to distinguished points in this solution space. For Hurwitz-Frobenius manifolds the action of a Legendre transformation on Hurwitz space data, and in particular the primary differential, is given.

analysisBasis.abstract: A theory of symmetries of generalized Frobenius manifolds is developed. This is used to study the solution space of all generalized Frobenius manifolds that are "above" a specific Frobenius manifold. Since all (semi-simple) Frobenius manifolds in 2-dimensions are known, by constructing all homogeneous Legendre fields associated to these manifolds we classify all 2-dimensional generalized Frobenius manifolds. With this description, the known examples of generalized Frobenius manifolds correspond to distinguished points in this solution space. For Hurwitz-Frobenius manifolds the action of a Legendre transformation on Hurwitz space data, and in particular the primary differential, is given.

metadata.title: Singular points of envelopes and offsets: a transition from 2D to 3D
metadata.abstract: We recall properties of the offsets of a (plane) kiss curve and their singularities, then we make a transition to 3D, considering the surface obtained by revolution of the kiss curve about one of its axes. When pos?sible, geometric constructions using automated methods are performed. This induces a need to focus on algebraic computations. Networking be?tween different kinds of software is of utmost importance, in order to use their respective strengths (dynamic geometry, dragging points, strong al?gebraic computations, etc.). A core difference between the 2D and 3D situations is that automated commands existing in 2D are not available in 3D. This makes the DGS less relevant in 3D than in 2D. In 3D, most of the work must be performed with the CAS. The singular points of a kiss curve in the plane are tacnodes (cusps) and crunodes (self-intersection). The singularities are not isolated anymore and cuspidal edges appear. In this setting, implicitization is a heavy endeavour and we need another technology, related to AI; we describe this briefly. The 2D activities have been proposed to in-service teachers learning towards an advanced degree.

metadata.abstract: Let $X:M^n\to\mathbb R^{n+1}$ be a complete self-shrinker with constant squared norm of the second fundamental form. metadata.title: Triviality of metric fibrations over locally finite metric graphs
metadata.abstract: In this note, we give a direct proof that every metric fibration over a geodesic metric space locally modeled on finite metric stars is isometrically isomorphic, over its base, to the $\ell^1$ product of its base and a fiber. metadata.title: Integrability of the horizontal mean curvature near characteristic points in the Heisenberg group
metadata.abstract: We investigate the local integrability of the horizontal mean curvature near characteristic points of surfaces in the first Heisenberg group. We prove that, for every embedded surface of class $C^{2,\alpha}$, with $\alpha>0$, the horizontal mean curvature is locally integrable with respect to (any) Riemannian surface measure, without any assumption on the structure of the characteristic set. We further establish that the horizontal unit normal belongs to $BV_{\mathrm{loc}}$ and characterize its $W^{1,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ regularity in terms of the vanishing one-dimensional Hausdorff measure of the characteristic set. Finally, we answer an open question by Danielli, Garofalo and Nhieu by constructing a $C^2$ surface with a unique characteristic point whose horizontal mean curvature fails to be locally integrable, thus showing that the additional Hölder regularity cannot, in general, be replaced by $C^2$ regularity.

metadata.title: Linear circle quotients of products of odd-dimensional spheres: classification and geometric applications
metadata.abstract: In this paper, we study the orbit manifolds of free diagonal linear circle actions on \(S^{2n+1}\times S^{2n+1}\). For every \(n\geq 1\), we establish a PL homeomorphism classification of the orbit manifolds in terms of the weights of the actions. We also obtain diffeomorphism classification and homotopy classification of such orbit manifolds in dimension $9$ and $13$. The diffeomorphism classification results lead to two geometric applications. For every \(m\geq 1\), there exist a non-spin \(9\)-manifold \(M_m^9\) and a spin \(13\)-manifold \(M_m^{13}\) in our family such that the moduli space of unit-volume homogeneous Einstein metrics on each manifold has at least \(2^{m-1}\) connected components. Moreover, each of these manifolds admits at least \(2^{m-1}\) regular Sasakian structures whose underlying contact structures are pairwise non-contactomorphic.

metadata.title: A counterexample to the strong version of the union of uniform closed balls conjecture in dimensions three and higher
metadata.abstract: Fifteen years after its formulation and following its recent proof in the plane, we show that the strong version of the union of uniform closed balls conjecture fails in every dimension $n\geq 3$. For every $n\geq 3$, $r>0$, and $\varepsilon>0$, we construct a compact set $S\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ satisfying the interior $r$-sphere condition and containing a point that belongs to no closed ball of radius $(1/2+\varepsilon)r$ contained in $S$. Consequently, the known universal radius $r/2$ is optimal in every dimension $n\geq 3$, even for compact sets, whereas the optimal radius in the plane is $r/\sqrt{3}$. The construction uses simplices with coincident circumcenter and incenter and yields an exact formula for the largest radius of a contained ball covering the center; the regular simplex recovers the original example motivating the conjecture.

analysisBasis.abstract: Fifteen years after its formulation and following its recent proof in the plane, we show that the strong version of the union of uniform closed balls conjecture fails in every dimension $n\geq 3$. For every $n\geq 3$, $r>0$, and $\varepsilon>0$, we construct a compact set $S\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ satisfying the interior $r$-sphere condition and containing a point that belongs to no closed ball of radius $(1/2+\varepsilon)r$ contained in $S$. Consequently, the known universal radius $r/2$ is optimal in every dimension $n\geq 3$, even for compact sets, whereas the optimal radius in the plane is $r/\sqrt{3}$. metadata.abstract: In this paper, we prove path connectedness of every nonempty strict Calabi-energy sublevel and identify the infimum of the square root of the Calabi energy over smooth metrics with the infimum of the descending Mabuchi slope in the metric completion. metadata.title: $φ$-symmetric Sasakian Lie algebras
metadata.abstract: We study Sasakian Lie algebras with trivial centre for which the adjoint operator $\mathrm{ad}_\xi$ associated to the Reeb vector field $\xi$ has two-dimensional image. Their structure is governed by a Kähler-exact Lie algebra $\mathfrak{h}_1$ and a vector $H_0\in\mathfrak{h}_1$, and the cases $H_0=0$ and $H_0\neq0$ are of a different nature. For $H_0=0$ we prove that the Sasakian structure is $\varphi$-symmetric if and only if $\mathfrak{h}_1$ is locally symmetric. For $H_0\neq0$ and $\mathfrak{h}_1$ solvable, we prove that it is $\varphi$-symmetric if and only if $\mathfrak{h}_1$ is locally symmetric and a natural two-form $\rho_0$ on $\mathfrak{h}_1$ determined by $H_0$ is parallel. The latter condition is equivalent to the vanishing of the mixed root spaces attached to the distinguished root selected by $H_0$ in the associated normal $j$-algebra. As a consequence, every Sasakian Lie algebra in this class of dimension at most seven is $\varphi$-symmetric, which extends a result of Loiudice and Lotta in dimension five. This bound is sharp: in dimension nine we exhibit a Sasakian structure which is not $\varphi$-symmetric, even though its Kähler base is locally symmetric.

metadata.title: LLM-Assisted Advances in the Ropelength Problem
metadata.abstract: This work summarizes some updates to the ropelength problem, concerning the shortest possible contour length of a unit-thickness knot, that were derived with the assistance of ChatGPT-5.6 Luna. The first of two main results is that the universal lower bound for a knot with crossing number C has been improved from $L\geq1.105C^{3/4}$ to $L\geq2.0996C^{3/4}$, achieved by further separating local and global terms in an optimization integral. The second main result is a bound relating ropelength to stick number (s), such that $L\geq\pi(s-1)$. This implies stronger lower bounds for the ropelengths of at least 41 torus knots, and a specific class of pretzel knots. Other results include an improved packing-based lower bound for T(Q,Q) links and an optimized standard parameterization for torus knots. There were many problems for which the LLM was unable to render assistance, for example in reducing the numerical coefficients or scalings of known universal upper bounds.

metadata.title: Regularity via subequations
metadata.abstract: Is there a unified theory of a priori estimates for purely second-order constant coefficient elliptic PDE? A strong indication that such a theory exists is provided by the foundational a priori estimates of Caffarelli--Nirenberg--Spruck (1984) and Trudinger (1995) that treated many equations, yet left out many others. This article develops such a unified theory based on Harvey--Lawson's theory of subequations, the aforementioned a priori estimates, and some new ingredients. Serendipitously, this also solves a problem posed by Nirenberg (2007). In addition to unifying all previously known such estimates, we find a vast number of new a priori estimates (e.g., spanning real, complex, quaternionic, $G_2$, among other natural equations, and even differential inclusions that generalize PDEs).

metadata.title: Thales's theorem in higher dimensions
metadata.abstract: In the Euclidean plane, Thales's theorem is equivalent to the statement that a quadrilateral with two opposite right angles has a circumscribed circle. We generalize the latter to higher dimensions: a convex polytope with two distinguished vertices, the \emph{poles}, such that the faces spanned by the two poles are perpendicular, is inscribed in the sphere whose diameter joins its poles. These \emph{orthogonally bipolar} polytopes are exactly the bipolar polytopes of a companion paper that arise as cutouts by orthogonal projections. As an application we show that for a polytope $P$ and a point $B$, the balls with diameters $[V,B]$, $V$ a vertex of $P$, cover $P$, and that the power diagram of their boundary spheres refines this covering to a tiling. Further, we investigate the properties of orthogonally bipolar polytopes, their characterization, and their application to tilings: in dimension three, the cutouts of $P$ by the orthogonal projections of $B$ onto its faces tile $P$ by orthogonally bipolar polytopes exactly when every such projection lies in the relative interior of its face. Finally, we propose an interpretation of the topic in political science.

metadata.abstract: For every complex simple Lie group G (not of type $E_8$) we construct the minimal Slodowy slice, which is a half-dimensional slice in the character variety of a closed surface group into G, containing the composition of Fuchsian representations with the minimal representation of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ in G and invariant under the mapping class group action. metadata.title: Rectifiable measures in Ahlfors regular spaces: endpoint constructions
metadata.abstract: A theorem of Balka and Keleti implies that on any complete separable metric space $\mathbb{X}$, every locally finite Borel measure $\mu$ of packing dimension strictly less than $m$ is "Euclidean-like" insofar as there exist Lipschitz maps $f_i:E_i\subset\mathbb{R}^m\rightarrow\mathbb{X}$ such that $\mu(\mathbb{X}\setminus\bigcup_1^\infty f_i(E_i))=0$. An ongoing challenge in geometric measure theory is to understand when this property, called $m$-rectifiability, holds for measures of packing dimension $m$. Towards this goal, we prove that every complete Ahlfors $q$-regular metric space with $q\geq m$ supports $m$-rectifiable doubling measures of packing dimension $m$. The proof of existence of such measures is new even when $\mathbb{X}=\mathbb{R}^n$ and $n>m$. More generally, on every complete Ahlfors $q$-regular metric space with $q>m-1$, we construct $m$-rectifiable, purely $(m-1)$-unrectifiable measures with any prescribed exact Hausdorff and packing dimensions $0\leq s_H\leq s_P\leq q$ with $m-1\leq s_P\leq m$, which are doubling when $s_H>0$. This verifies a conjecture of Badger and Schul. The design of the measures relies on metric cubes with variable scaling, in which the ratio of consecutive side lengths tends to infinity but jumps only on a sparse set of generations, together with Badger and Schul's square packing construction of Lipschitz maps.

metadata.title: No 13-vertex triangulation of the three-torus
metadata.abstract: Kühnel and Lassmann constructed a neighborly triangulation of the three-torus on 15 vertices, and Lutz conjectured that it is vertex-minimal. The standard lower-bound arguments exclude at most twelve vertices but do not decide the 13- and 14-vertex cases. We exclude the 13-vertex case. Our proof uses the Novik--Swartz $g_2$-inequality and a simplicial-complement reduction to a nine-vertex model of the punctured three-torus. By analyzing fundamental groups of small simplicial complexes and applying Alexander duality in a vertex link, we obtain a contradiction from the deficiency of $\Z^3$.

metadata.title: On the topology of some linear systems of hyperelliptic curves in Hirzebruch surfaces
metadata.abstract: Following a program suggested by Dolgachev and Libgober in 1981, we study the topology of the locus of smooth sections of linear systems of hyperelliptic curves on Hirzebruch surfaces. Within this class of examples, we find that a variety of behaviors occur - in some situations the enriched monodromy faithfully captures the fundamental group, and in others it does not. metadata.title: Bi-Hamiltonian structure and conserved quantities of the Yajima-Oikawa-Newell system
metadata.abstract:
We study the Hamiltonian and bi-Hamiltonian structure of the Yajima-Oikawa-Newell (YON) system, an integrable model of long wave-short wave interaction depending on two real parameters $\alpha$ and $ eta$, which reduces to the Yajima-Oikawa system for $\alpha=0$ and to the Newell system for $ eta=0$. For $\alpha
eq0$, a constant shift of the long wave maps the YON system into the Newell system, for which two nonlocal Hamiltonian operators are known. We show that, for $\alpha
eq0$, the system admits no local Hamiltonian operator homogeneous in its natural grading and polynomial in $ eta$. A nonlocal gauge transformation built on the potential of the long wave makes the first of the known operators local for a single value of its parameter: the transformed system is Hamiltonian, for every $\alpha
eq0$ and every $ eta$, with respect to a local, non-degenerate Poisson operator, which is the Lie-Poisson structure of the $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$ current algebra. From a recursion operator advancing the hierarchy by two steps, given in explicit weakly nonlocal form, we construct a second, weakly nonlocal Hamiltonian structure, whose nonlocal tail is generated by the three autonomous Lie point symmetries of the system, and prove that both structures are compatible. Since the recursion operator admits no square root and the first structure has no Casimirs, the Lenard-Magri chain splits into two families, seeded by the two simplest conserved quantities. Every flow of both families is local, and all the corresponding Hamiltonians are in involution. As by-products, we relate the Lie point symmetries of the system to its conserved quantities via Noether's theorem, and obtain the conserved densities in closed form by asymptotic diagonalisation of the Lax pair.

metadata.title: Regularity of $Q$-valued $C^1$ harmonic functions with applications to stable minimal hypersurfaces
metadata.abstract: We show that the derivative of a $Q$-valued $C^1$ function on an $n$-dimensional domain that is locally harmonic on its regular set is locally Dirichlet minimising, and that its branch set coincides with that of its derivative. As a consequence, we get that a $Q$-valued $C^1$ harmonic function is $C^{1,\alpha}$ and that its branch set is countably $(n-2)$-rectifiable when $n\geq 3$ and discrete when $n=2$. Our methods are directly applicable to the regularity theory of stable minimal hypersurfaces. We show that a multi-valued Lipschitz function whose graph is a two-sided, properly immersed, stable minimal $n$-dimensional hypersurface with locally $\mathcal{H}^{n-2}$-finite singular set, and whose Lipschitz constant is sufficiently small is in fact multi-valued $C^{1,\alpha}$. As a consequence, we obtain optimal regularity conclusions for a branched sheeting theorem of Bellettini for singular immersions. When $n=2$, we obtain stronger conclusions and show that locally about a branch point, a $Q$-valued $C^1$ harmonic function is the real part of a Dirichlet minimiser which is itself obtained from a finite number of holomorphic functions via classical branching, thus giving a full series expansion for the function near the branch point. Furthermore, we prove that the class of branched, two-sided, properly immersed, stable minimal surfaces with isolated singularities is compact under varifold convergence.

analysisBasis.abstract: We show that the derivative of a $Q$-valued $C^1$ function on an $n$-dimensional domain that is locally harmonic on its regular set is locally Dirichlet minimising, and that its branch set coincides with that of its derivative. As a consequence, we get that a $Q$-valued $C^1$ harmonic function is $C^{1,\alpha}$ and that its branch set is countably $(n-2)$-rectifiable when $n\geq 3$ and discrete when $n=2$. Our methods are directly applicable to the regularity theory of stable minimal hypersurfaces. We show that a multi-valued Lipschitz function whose graph is a two-sided, properly immersed, stable minimal $n$-dimensional hypersurface with locally $\mathcal{H}^{n-2}$-finite singular set, and whose Lipschitz constant is sufficiently small is in fact multi-valued $C^{1,\alpha}$. As a consequence, we obtain optimal regularity conclusions for a branched sheeting theorem of Bellettini for singular immersions. When $n=2$, we obtain stronger conclusions and show that locally about a branch point, a $Q$-valued $C^1$ harmonic function is the real part of a Dirichlet minimiser which is itself obtained from a finite number of holomorphic functions via classical branching, thus giving a full series expansion for the function near the branch point. Furthermore, we prove that the class of branched, two-sided, properly immersed, stable minimal surfaces with isolated singularities is compact under varifold convergence.

metadata.title: Explicit restricted isometries with $k=m^{2/3-o(1)}$
metadata.abstract: We construct an explicit family of real $m\times n$ restricted isometries with $m\to\infty$, $m/n\to 0$, $\delta_k\to 0$, and $k=m^{2/3-o(1)}$. We combine Gershgorin's circle theorem with a flat RIP estimate to reduce the problem to choosing a large vertex set in a strongly regular graph with the property that every small subset spans few edges. We select this vertex set using an incidence geometric result due to Zahl. The proof only uses the entrywise absolute value of the Gram matrix despite the conventional wisdom that such proof techniques exhibit a barrier of $m^{1/2}$. We prove that this barrier is actually $m^{2/3}$, and we show that our particular construction exhibits the same barrier.

metadata.title: $G_2'$-Slodowy Slices II: Anosov Representations
metadata.abstract: We find \emph{exotic} connected components of Anosov representations of surface groups in the higher rank group $G=G_2'$ that are neither $\iota$-Fuchsian deformations nor higher rank Teichmüller spaces. These representations are found through the non-abelian Hodge correspondence via $G_2'$-Higgs bundles that we call \emph{$\alpha$-bundles} and \emph{$\beta$-bundles}, which are particular cyclic Higgs bundles in the Slodowy slices of the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-triples associated to the simple roots $\alpha$ and $\beta$ of $\mathfrak{g}_2^{\mathbb{C}}$. We first prove that (most) $\beta$-bundles that are also Hodge bundles are $P_{\beta}$-Anosov and $\alpha$-bundles are $P_{\alpha}$-Anosov. The strategy employed is new, geometric, and general. For $\sigma \in \{\alpha, \beta\}$, we then show the locally homogeneous $(G_2', G_2'/P_{\sigma})$-manifold ${\mathscr{M}}_{\sigma}(\rho)$ recently described in arXiv:2510.12757 , for the representation $\rho:\pi_1S\rightarrow G_2'$ associated to a $\sigma$-bundle, coincides up to finite cover with the corresponding geometric structure for $\rho$ defined via domains of discontinuity by Guichard-Wienhard and Kapovich-Leeb-Porti. Consequently, we find that $\pi_1({\mathscr{M}}_{\sigma}(\rho))$ is an invariant for the connected component of $\rho$ in the space of $P_{\sigma}$-Anosov representations. After verifying the folklore result that the $G_2'$-character variety has exactly three connected components, we conclude lower bounds for the number of connected components of $P_{\sigma}$-Anosov representations in the two non-Hitchin components, most of which are exotic.

metadata.title: Local Rigidity of Bergman Logarithmic Flatness on Compact Hermitian Symmetric Spaces
metadata.abstract: We prove the local rigidity of Bergman logarithmic flatness near the standard metrics associated with fixed invariant positive polarizations on compact Hermitian symmetric spaces. Every sufficiently small smooth deformation preserving Bergman logarithmic flatness is induced by a holomorphic automorphism and a constant rescaling. This establishes a Bergman analogue of the local rigidity results for Szegő logarithmic flatness obtained by Lu--Tian (Duke Math. J., 2004) and, more recently, Loi--Palmieri--Zuddas (2026).
